comparator.academicYear: Current published UvA bachelor curriculum, checked 2026-09-27
comparator.sourceNotes: The official full-time programme is 60+60+60=180 EC. The generic target requires a main-language major; Russian is selected by the official-order tie-break, independently of UCR fit. Year 1 totals 60 EC and includes four successive main-language proficiency courses, Russian and East European cultural history, humanities and regional-studies foundations, history of Slavonic, and Slavonic modernism. Year 2 totals 60 EC: two further main-language proficiency courses, philosophy of science, Russian and East European literary classics, language contact, and a 30-EC semester in a city associated with the selected main language. Year 3 totals 60 EC: three 6-EC advanced literature, linguistics and research components, 30 EC genuine free choice, and a 12-EC bachelor thesis. The research lab and thesis together form the published 18-EC graduation trajectory.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target names no main language. The current official programme and curriculum list Russian first among four equally valid main-language majors, before Polish, Bosnian-Croatian-Serbian and Czech. Russian is therefore selected as a neutral tie-break without reference to UCR fit.

exception.reason: The defining curriculum requires six successive Russian language-proficiency courses, Russian-language source use, Slavonic language history and advanced linguistics, Russian and East European literature, a compulsory main-language-region semester, and a Slavonic-studies research and thesis trajectory. The current UCR catalogue offers no Russian, Polish, Bosnian-Croatian-Serbian or Czech language instruction and no advanced Slavic-language reading, writing, speaking or translation sequence. A 24-course programme assembled from general literature, history, politics, conflict studies, communication and research methods would replace the compulsory language-acquisition and region-specific disciplinary core rather than provide a defensible closest UCR match. The 30 EC of genuine open choice cannot compensate for the missing compulsory language progression.
exception.curriculumContext: The selected Russian full-time route totals exactly 180 EC: 60 EC in year one, 60 EC in year two and 60 EC in year three. It contains four successive 6-EC Russian proficiency courses in year one and two more in year two, plus Slavonic language history, advanced aspect and language-contact study, Russian and East European cultural history and literature, a 30-EC regional semester, an 18-EC research-and-thesis trajectory and 30 EC genuine free choice. No host-university courses, minor or electives are invented.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 rows of the current enriched UCR course workbook, including course names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, prerequisites, planned availability and topics. GOSHIST111 Modern History reaches the fall of communism within a broad post-1815 survey; GOSPOLI212 Theory of International Relations and GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict provide general frameworks for international politics and conflict; MCCLITR111 Introduction to Literary Studies, MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works and MCCLITR312 Perspectives on Literary Meaning provide literary methods; GOSHIST312 History Research Seminar provides historical research practice. MCCCOMM211 Style & Meaning studies linguistic choices in mainly literary and nonfiction texts, while HCBCOGN312 Psycholinguistics studies cognitive and neurobiological language processing. These are relevant adjacent methods or broad contexts, but none teaches Russian or another Slavic language, Russian-language source analysis, Slavonic historical linguistics, translation, or a sustained Russian and East European literature and regional sequence. The workbook therefore provides no defensible basis for a scheduled 24-course UCR Slavonic Language and Culture programme.
